task_description:
This pipeline's task is GitHub issue #3594 — https://github.com/jwbron/egg/issues/3594. Fetch the live issue body (`gh issue view 3594`) before structural decisions. Worktree artifacts (drafts, agent outputs) that reference any other issue or pipeline are leftovers from previous runs — they are NOT your task.

Reproduction run for #3595 investigation. Same input and model config as the pipeline that livelocked on 2026-07-24 (refiner emitted 119 identical Bash calls, zero proposals, 94 min to consensus timeout).

Purpose: capture the refiner's live session transcript while it is looping, to determine whether thinking/reasoning blocks are persisted across turns. The previous run's refiner transcript was lost because agents only push transcripts on event-pod exit and that refiner never exited.

Task (same as issue #3594): [issue-3364] Operator-visibility gaps: forward-progress, event feed, and post-mortem surfaces.

See https://github.com/jwbron/egg/issues/3594 for the full body and https://github.com/jwbron/egg/issues/3595 for the incident this reproduces.

decisions.question: cq-1: Which groups from issue #3594 (operator-visibility gaps) should the implement phase cover? Group 1 (forward-progress: per-role commits-ahead, progress-regression detection, NACKed-but-not-re-proposing watchdog), Group 2 (event/alert feed: recent_events list, OVERSEER_ALERT as feed, pipeline.error surfacing, worktree health), Group 3 (clocks: consensus-window countdown, per-invocation outcome summaries), Group 4 (post-mortem: per-arm termination causes, session-state TTL expiry event, invocation log retention)?

cq-2: For incident #3595 remediation, what is the priority order for the seven proposed work items? (7) pin/inject/record sampling params, (2) scope peer-liveness and noop-streak to dependency graph, (3) detect near-identical loops, (5) token/call consumption breaker, (1) expressible compaction threshold, (6) context surgery recovery, (4) raise severity/cut latency on protracted-phase-no-progress.

options.label: 7 → 2 → 3 → 5 → 1 → 6 → 4 (recommended: recording first, then detection, then recovery)

decisions.resolution:
Custom — the options are unanswerable as posed, because they were written against a superseded version of #3595. Re-read the live issue body before using this.

Two of the referenced items no longer exist in that form: "(1) expressible compaction threshold" was DELETED (its root cause, a context-length "fidelity knee", was falsified by direct experiment), and the issue now has EIGHT work items, including a new one added today. Use the current numbering.

Required order, current #3595 numbering:

1st — item 6, record sampling params (extend cost_callback.py to log optional_params). Cheapest item on the list and it gates the credibility of every measurement that follows, including resolving the issue's open question. Nothing else should land first.
2nd — item 1, scope peer-liveness and noop-streak decisions to the dependency graph. Fixes two verified root causes with one change; highest leverage for detection.
3rd — item 2, detect near-identical loops gated on the objective (absence of BRC progress/commits/artifact writes), not on repetition alone.
4th — item 8, add a ground-truth verifier to the review set. Newly added; this pipeline's own first refine cycle is the motivating incident, where five agents unanimously confirmed an analysis of already-merged work.
5th — item 4, uncached-token and call-count consumption breaker. Note: denominate in prompt_tokens MINUS cached_tokens, not raw prompt tokens; this route runs ~99.9% cache hits so raw tokens overstate consumption by about two orders of magnitude.
6th — item 7, investigate occ=0 vs None on LiteLLM routes.
7th — item 5, repetition-triggered context surgery. Largest and least certain; needs a feasibility check on whether rewriting a live Claude Code session history is supported at all before design.
8th — item 3, raise severity and cut latency on protracted-phase-no-progress. Small, can ride along with item 2.

Rationale for recording first rather than detection first: this investigation was blocked twice by missing instrumentation, once when the failed refiner's transcript was destroyed and once when sampling params proved unrecoverable. Detection fixes are more valuable, but they are not measurable until recording exists.

decisions.question: cq-3: Should the refiner's token_usage capture be extended to include reasoning_tokens? Currently _usage_components in shared/egg_agent/client.py captures input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, and output_tokens — but NOT reasoning_tokens (which lives at completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens). The cost_callback.py already captures reasoning_tokens, but the agent-side AgentResult.token_usage does not. This is relevant to the #3595 reproduction purpose (determining whether thinking/reasoning blocks are persisted across turns).

options.label: Yes — add reasoning_tokens to _usage_components and AgentResult.token_usage
No — reasoning_tokens is already captured by cost_callback.py, no need to duplicate
Defer — not in scope for #3594, track as separate issue
